headline: High risk of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors from shared project/workspace files and broad tool access; Roo Code’s MCP/browser surface increases exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both agents can read and write shared project/workspace files, so one agent can ingest the other’s outputs as trusted content. gpt-engineer writes files in a project directory, and Roo Code shares state via filesystem and can use MCP/browser surfaces, making instruction-hijack via file content plausible in default use.
conditions: IF either agent reads the other’s generated files as instructions without provenance checks, injection is possible.
IF the two agents operate in the same project/workspace directory, shared-file prompt injection becomes reachable.
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories/workspaces.
Add a manual review step before either agent consumes the other’s files.
Prefix machine-generated files with a non-executable marker and ignore it in prompts.
Disable MCP inputs for the Roo Code session when not needed.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging and parser hardening for agent-generated content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch source code/project files, and both have broad network egress to configured model APIs. Because Roo Code can also use MCP servers and browser screenshots, sensitive workspace content can flow outward if either agent is pointed at secrets or private code in the shared workspace.
conditions: IF sensitive code or secrets are present in the shared workspace, both agents can access them.
IF Roo Code is configured with an MCP server or browser workflow that transmits context, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared workspace.
Use separate least-privilege API keys for each agent.
Disable browser/screenshot workflows unless required.
Restrict outbound network destinations at the host or proxy.
requires-engineering: add workspace redaction and egress allowlisting.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted filesystem write to the same project/workspace, and Roo Code also modifies git state. gpt-engineer writes files then offers to run, while Roo Code approves tool actions per step; concurrent edits can clobber files or corrupt git history in default shared-workspace use.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same directory, write-write conflicts are possible.
IF Roo Code commits or rewrites git state while gpt-engineer is generating files, repository corruption or lost work can occur.
mitigations: Run the agents in separate worktrees or directories.
Serialize access with a human-controlled lock file.
Avoid git commits while both agents are active.
Review diffs before applying either agent’s changes.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking around shared mutable state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-engineer explicitly writes files then offers to run, and Roo Code can act on workspace content with browser/MCP/tooling. If Roo Code treats gpt-engineer’s generated code or notes as authoritative, errors can cascade into unsafe edits, execution, or external actions without verification.
conditions: IF Roo Code consumes gpt-engineer output without independent validation, downstream mistakes can propagate.
IF either agent executes generated code from the other, a bad assumption can become an action.
mitigations: Require a human review before execution or commit.
Insert a validation step between generation and action.
Use tests or linting before accepting generated changes.
Disable automatic execution of generated code.
requires-engineering: add structured handoff contracts with verification gates.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source coding agents with docs-only evidence and no explicit residency or certification mismatch is stated. The main compliance concern is operational: Roo Code’s browser/screenshots and broader egress can widen data handling scope, but the profiles do not prove a specific residency or regulated-data violation.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into the shared workspace or browser flow, compliance review is needed.
IF a deployment requires residency or retention guarantees, the profiles do not document them.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in the workspace.
Disable browser capture for sensitive tasks.
Confirm retention settings for the configured model provider.
Document data handling boundaries for both agents.
requires-engineering: obtain vendor compliance attestations before regulated use.
